header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.tamil_translation: (migrating), came to Madinah Munawwarah, (one day) the Muhajirin (the people of Makkah) came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Rasulullah, we have never seen anyone like these people to whom we have come (the people of Madinah, the Ansar). When they are wealthy, they spend generously. Even when they face hardship, they give us comfort and help. In the labour and the toil they take our share upon themselves as well, and they make us partners in the profit. (Because of this ordinary practice of theirs of giving others preference over themselves) we fear that all the reward and recompense will go to them alone (and that we will be left without reward in the Hereafter).” The Prophet ﷺ replied: “No! It is not so! As long as you make “du'a” for them in return for this favour and keep praising them (keep thanking them), it cannot become like that.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: مَنْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ رَيْحَانٌ فَلَا يَرُدُّهُ فَاِنَّهُ خَفِيْفُ الْمَحْمِلِ طَيِّبُ الرِّيْحِ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم باب استعمال المسك... رقم: ٥٨٨٣
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said: “If anyone is given a fragrant flower as a gift, he should not refuse it, for it is a very ordinary thing of little value. And it gives off a very pleasant fragrance.”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- If someone refuses to accept a thing of little value such as a flower, the one giving it may be hurt at heart, thinking: “He refuses to accept it only because my thing is of no value.”
(Ma'ariful Hadith)
